findings.what: A 409 'a classification run is already in progress' is rendered to the user as 'the run FAILED and saved nothing', with an active button that will 409 again.
findings.why_it_is_silent: startRun returns json({ error: 'ritzat-nituach kvar poelet.', run_id, status: 'running' }, 409) at index.ts:825-828. classify() tests `if (result?.status) setLocal(result)` BEFORE looking at result.error, so status:'running' wins and the error string is discarded. localState() has branches for 'partial' (line 91), 'done' (101) and 'noop' (110) only; 'running' falls through to the final branch, which paints the Hebrew sentence for a FAILED run plus the sub-line 'a failed run cannot be continued' plus an ACTIVE 'run analysis' button. The truth is the opposite: a run IS alive and IS writing rows (writeInsight upserts per batch, index.ts:472-479). The screen lies and does not fail - the module's own 4.3 sentence. serverRunState() DOES handle 'running' correctly (line 137), but only for meta.run_in_progress, which is a payload snapshot; it cannot see a run that started after the payload loaded - which is exactly the scenario the file header (lines 19-25) says was the blind spot it closed.

findings.what: The Excel export's only realistic failure is an unhandled promise rejection: the click does nothing, nothing is shown, nothing is logged.
findings.why_it_is_silent: exportReportRows() ends with `return writeXlsxFile(...)` (reportsExport.js:195). Every overload of writeXlsxFile is declared Promise<void>/Promise<Blob> (node_modules/write-excel-file/index.d.ts:184-195). handleExport() calls it WITHOUT await inside try{} (ExportBar.jsx:28-31), so a library/Blob/download failure rejects outside the try and never reaches setError - no alert, no console, no clue. The two synchronous throws the catch CAN see (EXPORT_NO_TABLE, EXPORT_NO_ROWS at reportsExport.js:192-193) are already prevented from firing, because exportCaption() sets disabled:true for both cases (reportsExport.js:97-102) and the Button is disabled={caption.disabled} (ExportBar.jsx:41). So the whole handler guards a path that cannot happen, while the path that can happen is unguarded.

findings.what: `const known = [caption.file, err?.message].includes(err?.message)` is a tautology - always true.
findings.why_it_is_silent: The array literally contains err?.message, so .includes(err?.message) can never be false (strings and undefined both match). Consequences: (a) the generic Hebrew fallback on line 33 is unreachable, and the intent stated in the comment on line 31 - do not leak technical text to the screen - never fires, so raw English library text would print verbatim into a Hebrew screen; (b) a throw with no message sets error=undefined, which is falsy, so the {error && ...} alert renders NOTHING - a caught error with nothing on screen. Same handler as S3B-2, separate defect.

findings.what: A payload that declares meta.missing_params AND has zero rows never shows the 'missing system parameter' line - it shows the empty envelope instead.
findings.why_it_is_silent: `if (isEmptyPage) return <EmptyPage .../>` at line 607 returns before <MissingParamsBanner names={payload.meta?.missing_params}/> at line 640 is reached. isEmptyAfterLoad (line 380) fires when rows.length===0 && (population.n===0 || customerId). So the user reads 'no data yet' / 'no data for the selected customer' when the truth is 'a params row is missing and this page could not compute'. That is the exact failure 7.83 / C5 forbid (a missing params row must surface, never a silent default), and it is the same lie the module's 4.3 doctrine names - the screen does not fail, it reports emptiness. The same gap exists on the error and noPermission branches (lines 549-566), which is defensible there because no payload is in hand - but NOT on the empty branch, where a payload carrying a declared missing param IS in hand and is discarded.

findings.what: The module's only edge-function call discards the original error with no log of any kind.
findings.why_it_is_silent: `try { return await error.context.json() } catch { return { error: GENERIC_ERROR } }` - the bare catch drops both the parse error AND the outer supabase error object (FunctionsFetchError / FunctionsRelayError / FunctionsHttpError). A CORS failure, a gateway 502, a DNS failure and a malformed body all collapse into the identical Hebrew sentence with nothing written anywhere. Measured contrast in the same module: ReportSurface.jsx:514 logs console.error with the RPC name, ReportsPage.jsx:241 logs console.warn. A full grep for console. across src/modules/11_reports/ and src/lib/reports*.js returns exactly those two lines - this call site is the only network path in m11 with zero diagnostic trace. Six months from now there is nothing to debug from.

findings.what: setError(err?.message ?? GENERIC_ERROR) - the nullish operator does not catch an empty-string message, so an error can clear pending and say nothing.
findings.why_it_is_silent:
'' ?? X is '', not X. error='' is falsy, so the {error &&

} block (lines 279-283) renders nothing, while finally{setPending(false)} re-enables the button. The user sees the button come back and no message: the click looks like it did nothing. Low probability today (invokeClassify swallows rather than throws, and toError always sets a message), but it is the classic nullish-instead-of-or trap sitting on the one write path in the module. || would be correct here precisely because an empty message is not a usable message.

findings.what: A door whose target is not in the catalog is a dead click - no navigation, no message, no log. Two sources side by side, not a patch instruction.
findings.why_it_is_silent: `if (!door || !canOpenTab(door.tab, permissions)) return`. SOURCE A (the code's own recorded reasoning, ReportsPage.jsx:385-396): a target that is not in the catalog deliberately STAYS a visible door, because openDoor stops it without navigating, and hiding it would swallow a payload defect into a screen that looks fine. SOURCE B (this module's own doctrine, quoted in api.js:36-38, rule 14b-3): a row that looks clickable and leads nowhere is a dead marker, which is the whole reason ROW_DOOR_KINDS exists. The recorded decision settles 'do not hide the door'; it does not say the user should get zero feedback and no console trace when the payload has drifted. The permission half is separately handled and is fine: canOpenTarget (line 396) keeps a permission-blocked TILE door from rendering as a door at all, and a permission-blocked ROW door navigates into ProtectedRoute, which states the block.

confirmed_by_design.what: 42501 / RLS denial reaches a dedicated permission envelope and is NEVER painted as an empty report. This is the highest-value item in the brief and it is done right on every one of the 16 surfaces.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: toScreenError maps err.code==='42501' to {kind:'noPermission'} and the branch order puts noPermission BEFORE error (Envelope.jsx:54-56: merging a permission block into 'error' would hide it behind a retry button that can never help). Failure keeps payload:null - never {} or [] - so section 4.3 of the root CLAUDE.md holds. Blind spot CLOSED by measurement this turn: grep -rn callReport over src/ (non-test) returns exactly two lines - api.js:152 (the definition) and ReportSurface.jsx:497 (the only call site) - and reportsCatalog.js declares 16 rpc: entries, so no surface bypasses this mapping.

confirmed_by_design.what: listCustomers() returns [] with error:null for RECRUIT/STAFF and the picker degrades to 'all customers' only - a RECORDED decision, not a defect.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: docs/micro_guides/module-11.md:706 D-16 - the customer filter list is a second RLS-gated read, RECRUIT/STAFF get [] with error:null, the foundation degrades honestly, and the right fix (a gated customer list from a report RPC) is a decision registered as m11 debt in Phase 4, not patched. Confirmed in code: the empty list does not hide the picker, does not raise an error, and the reports still run. One honest measurement beside it, for the record and NOT as a fix instruction: the honesty is the ABSENCE of options - there is no sentence on screen saying the filter is unavailable in this role, because customerDisabledReason is driven only by meta.customer_filter_ignored (ReportsPage.jsx:136, 345), never by an empty list. The .catch on line 239 also logs console.warn and sets [] - correct here, because this list is an aid and not the report.

confirmed_by_design.what: The report shape gate throws loudly instead of rendering a half-payload.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: The gate does not 'repair' and does not fill defaults - a missing answer is a broken contract, and a screen that invents a missing structure shows empty tiles as if they had been measured. A missing key throws REPORT_SHAPE_DRIFT with a Hebrew message; all four params are always sent even when null, so a renamed signature errors loudly instead of silently answering for the wrong period.

confirmed_by_design.what: The one write RPC checks the answer, not the absence of an error.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: `if (data?.ok !== true) throw` - the row-count-equivalent check section 4.3 demands. AnalysisRunBar.jsx:248-250 then shows the P0001 Hebrew message from the DB as-is.

confirmed_by_design.what: Both halves of the failed-run contract verified - the function records failure honestly and the UI branches on body.status, never on res.ok.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: finishRun writes the run row BEFORE returning on every path, because a run left 'running' after the function returned would block every future run with nobody to release it. nothingSaved means 'failed', a partial save means 'partial' - never 'partial' with zero rows, which approve_feedback_ai_run would have let through. executeRun closes the run row and re-throws rather than swallowing. On the UI side invokeClassify reads error.context.json() so a non-2xx body still reaches the branch, and classify() tests result.status. ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE BRIEF'S WORDING, measured not assumed: the fatal path returns HTTP 502 with status:'failed' (index.ts:656-660), not HTTP 200; only the non-fatal nothing-saved path returns 200 + status:'failed' (index.ts:667, 674-678). The UI is robust to both, so the contract holds in effect - but 'HTTP 200 with status:failed' is true of one of the two failed exits, not both.

confirmed_by_design.what: Every write in the edge function checks row count, exactly as section 4.3 requires.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: The header comment states the rule verbatim: a blocked write returns {data:null, error:null} on all three verbs, and .select() plus a length check is the difference between 'saved' and 'the screen lied'. Each write does .select() and throws on !data || data.length === 0. The double-run gate deliberately runs as service-role and says why: an RLS-blocked read returns zero rows with error:null, and zero rows there reads as 'no active run' - so the very check meant to prevent a double run would have been the one permitting it. loadCandidates even enforces an explicit row cap because PostgREST truncates at 1,000 rows without an error. This is the best error handling in the module.

confirmed_by_design.what: The m4 invite insert does check row count, in effect - a blocked write is counted as a failure, not as a success.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: writeAssignmentRow is .insert(row).select().maybeSingle(); an RLS-blocked insert yields {data:null,error:null}, and `return error ? null : data` returns null, which the caller reads as !inserted so outcome.failed += 1. writeInviteToken - untouched by m11 - is .select() plus Boolean(updated?.length). Both honour the 4.3 addendum.

confirmed_by_design.what: The recommended_rank write falls back to NULL on failure - a documented, spec-quoted fallback, not a silent one.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: Card t5, quoted verbatim in the why-comment: if the write fails the invite does NOT fail because of it - NULL is recorded and a console.warn is emitted. The code warns with the hostess id and the project id, and isRankWriteFailure deliberately EXCLUDES 23505 so the triple-key race retry is not swallowed. Residual worth naming once, not a fix: the user is never told, so report 14a (adoption-of-recommendation) under-counts by exactly the number of warned rows, and the only trace is a browser console line nobody reads. That consequence is the price the recorded ruling chose.

confirmed_by_design.what: A chart that came back with no data says so in words instead of drawing an empty frame.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: Recorded and measured 16/09/2026: one click on the 'this month' pill in m14 left a 260px frame completely empty, with no word, no legend and no screen-reader table. Legend, LTR wrapper and the screen-reader twin table are all suppressed when data.length === 0, because all three describe data that is not there.

confirmed_by_design.what: parseDrill's bare catch returning null is deliberate URL robustness, not a swallowed error.
confirmed_by_design.ruling: A malformed address does not bring down a screen - it is read as the root, exactly like a foreign tab value falling to the first tab (S-18). A malformed ?drill= is user-supplied input, not a system failure, and falling back to the root level shows real root data.
